opportunities.name: Pull a country's GDP and population from the World Bank and email a client brief
opportunities.description: In the World Bank Data tab, click the search box, type {country} and press Enter; open the {country} country page -> Note the latest GDP (current US$) and population figures with their year -> Scroll down to GDP growth (annual %) and note the latest value -> Switch to the Wikipedia tab, search "{country}" and open the article; note the capital and the currency from the infobox -> Switch to the Mail tab, click To and type {client}@example.com, click Subject and type "{country} macro snapshot" -> Click Body and type "Hi {client}, {country}: GDP <gdp> (<year>), growth <growth>%, population <population>; capital <capital>, currency <currency>." Do not click Send. Click Discard
steps: In the World Bank Data tab, click the search box, type {country} and press Enter; open the {country} country page
Note the latest GDP (current US$) and population figures with their year
Scroll down to GDP growth (annual %) and note the latest value
Switch to the Wikipedia tab, search "{country}" and open the article; note the capital and the currency from the infobox
Switch to the Mail tab, click To and type {client}@example.com, click Subject and type "{country} macro snapshot"
Click Body and type "Hi {client}, {country}: GDP <gdp> (<year>), growth <growth>%, population <population>; capital <capital>, currency <currency>." Do not click Send. Click Discard

opportunities.name: Add a public-domain classic to a reading list from Project Gutenberg and the author's Wikipedia page
opportunities.description: In the Project Gutenberg tab, click the search box, type "{title}" and press Enter -> Open the matching book by {author}; on its page note the release date and the downloads count. Do not download it -> Switch to the Wikipedia tab, search "{author}" and open the article; note the birth and death years -> Switch to Notes, click "New note", type "Read: {title} by {author} (<birth>-<death>), Gutenberg since <release date>, <downloads> downloads" and press Enter
steps: In the Project Gutenberg tab, click the search box, type "{title}" and press Enter
Open the matching book by {author}; on its page note the release date and the downloads count. Do not download it
Switch to the Wikipedia tab, search "{author}" and open the article; note the birth and death years
Switch to Notes, click "New note", type "Read: {title} by {author} (<birth>-<death>), Gutenberg since <release date>, <downloads> downloads" and press Enter
